p.src: Now it happened that Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, ignored the warnings of Tang Bin and Geng Gong and led the commanders charging into the enemy formation. Qiao Daoqing trapped them with his sorcery, and more than five hundred men were captured alive; not one escaped. Seeing that matters had taken a bad turn, Geng Gong wheeled his horse eastward, lashed it twice, and fled ahead of the others. Tang Bin saw Li Kui and the others fall into the trap and the troops descend into confusion. When he also saw Geng Gong flee first, he thought, “Qiao Daoqing's magic is formidable. If I fail to escape, I shall only earn the scorn of others. I have heard that a soldier fears not death, but the loss of his honor. Now that matters have come to this, how can I cherish my life?” Ready to sacrifice his life, Tang Bin gripped his spear, spurred his horse, and charged into the fray. Seeing the ferocity of his charge, Qiao Daoqing hastily formed a hand seal and recited an incantation, then cried, “Haste!” At once, a cloud of yellow sand rose from within his formation and swept straight into Tang Bin's face. The sand blinded Tang Bin and left him helpless. The soldiers quickly overtook him, thrust a spear into his left leg, and toppled him from his horse; he too was taken alive. The northern army had a rule that anyone who delivered a captured officer alive received a double reward. That was why none of the commanders had been killed. Meanwhile, the ten thousand troops under Tang Bin were engulfed in yellow sand. Men were slain and horses brought down, and the force scattered like stars and clouds, losing more than half its soldiers.

p.src: Now Lin Chong and Xu Ning, stationed at the eastern gate, heard the din of battle rising to the heavens south of the city and hurriedly led their troops to the rescue. The defenders within the city, Sun Qi and the others, recognized Qiao Daoqing's banners and hastened to open the gate to receive him. Li Kui and his companions had already been carried captive into the city. Presently Geng Gong appeared with a few routed survivors, galloping so hard that they gasped for breath, their saddles awry, reins askew, and helmets tilted to one side. Only when they saw Lin Chong and Xu Ning did they rein in their horses. Lin Chong and Xu Ning hurriedly asked whose troops these were. Geng Gong, still reeling with panic, managed to stammer out a few words. The two men hastened back toward the main camp with him and happened to meet Wang Ying and Hu Sanniang returning from patrol with three hundred horsemen. On hearing the news, they all went together to report it to Vanguard Song. Geng Gong then related in full how Li Kui and the others had been captured by Qiao Daoqing. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed by the report and cried, “Li Kui and the others are doomed!” Wu Yong counseled him, “Brother, set aside your grief for now and attend quickly to the urgent matter. Since the enemy possesses sorcery, we must send at once to Huguan for Fan Rui to oppose him.” Song Jiang said, “Send for Fan Rui, but at the same time advance the army and demand that accursed Taoist return Li Kui and the others.” Wu Yong pleaded bitterly with him, but he would not listen.

p.src: Vanguard Song thereupon ordered Wu Yong to command the other officers and defend the camp. Song Jiang himself led eight commanders—Lin Chong, Xu Ning, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Liu Tang, Tang Long, Li Yun, and Yu Baosi—and twenty thousand troops, setting out at once to attack the southern side of Zhaode. Suo Chao and Zhang Qing came to meet them. The combined army advanced on the city, waving banners, beating drums, raising battle cries, and sounding gongs. Meanwhile, Qiao Daoqing entered the city and took his seat in the command headquarters. After Sun Qi and the other nine commanders had paid their respects, they were about to prepare a banquet for him when a scout suddenly reported that Song's army had returned. Qiao Daoqing said angrily, “What insolence from that fellow!” He said to Sun Qi, “Wait here until I return after capturing Song Jiang.” He immediately mounted his horse and led four subordinate commanders and three thousand troops out of the city to meet the enemy. Song's troops were forming ranks and issuing their challenge when the city gate opened and the drawbridge came down. A formidable body of troops surged out, led by a mounted adept—Qiao Daoqing, the “Demon Lord of Illusion”—who brandished his precious sword and led his men across the bridge. The two armies faced each other, their banners and drums in full view. Both sides trained powerful bows and heavy crossbows upon the opposing lines; war horns sounded between the formations, and battle drums thundered together. The gate banners in Song's formation parted, and Vanguard Song rode forth. Yu Baosi stood before his horse holding aloft the commander's banner. Lin Chong, Xu Ning, Lu Zhishen, and Liu Tang guarded him on the left, while Suo Chao, Zhang Qing, Wu Song, and Tang Long guarded him on the right. Vanguard Song, his breast filled with rage, pointed at Qiao Daoqing and cursed him: “You wicked Taoist who aids rebels, release my brothers and the more than five hundred men at once! Delay even a moment, and when I seize you, I shall hack your corpse into ten thousand pieces!” Daoqing shouted, “Song Jiang, curb your insolence! I will not return them. Let us see how you mean to capture me!” Song Jiang flew into a rage and pointed with the tip of his whip. Lin Chong, Xu Ning, Suo Chao, Zhang Qing, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and Liu Tang all charged forward together. Qiao Daoqing clicked his teeth to work his magic, formed a hand seal, and recited an incantation. Pointing his sword westward, he cried, “Haste!” In an instant, countless soldiers and commanders came flying from the west and threw Song's army into confusion. Qiao Daoqing then pointed his sword northward, muttered another spell, and cried, “Haste!” In a moment, heaven and earth grew dark and the sun lost its light. Sand flew, stones hurtled, the earth trembled, and the sky shook. Lin Chong and the other commanders were charging forward when they saw nothing before them but yellow sand and black vapor; not a single enemy soldier was visible. Song's army fell into disorder without even fighting, while the frightened horses beneath them bolted about and neighed wildly. Lin Chong and the others hurriedly wheeled their horses around, closed about Song Jiang to protect him, and fled northward. Qiao Daoqing summoned his troops to charge in pursuit. Song Jiang's forces were scattered like stars and clouds and broken into disconnected groups, men calling for their brothers and crying out as they searched for sons and fathers. Song Jiang and his men fled in confusion, but before they had gone half a li, a strange sight appeared ahead. The level, open plain across which their army had just come was now covered by a vast expanse of white, heaven-high waves stretching beyond the horizon like the great Eastern Ocean. Even had they grown wings from their ribs, they could not have flown across it. With enemy troops pursuing from behind, death seemed certain for them all. Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and Liu Tang cried out together, “Are we to let ourselves be bound without a fight?” The three summoned all their strength, turned back, and charged northward. Suddenly, a thunderclap burst forth, and more than twenty golden-armored divine warriors appeared in midair, raining blows upon them with their weapons. Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and Liu Tang were quickly struck down; the northern soldiers rushed up, and they too were captured alive. Another great shout rang out: “Song Jiang, dismount and submit to bondage, and your life shall be spared!” Song Jiang looked up to heaven and sighed: “My own death is of no consequence. p.src: Song Jiang and the others had already drawn their swords and were about to cut their own throats when a man suddenly rushed forward and stopped them, saying, “Do not do this. None of you need fear. My station is exalted among the powers of Earth. Seeing your loyalty and righteousness, I have come expressly to subdue this enchanted water and save you, that you may return to your stronghold.” When the commanders looked at him, they saw that his appearance was extraordinary: two fleshy horns grew from his head, his whole body was blue-black, his hair was red, and he was otherwise naked save for a pair of yellow breeches about his loins; in his left hand he held a bell. The man scooped up a handful of earth and cast it toward the towering, sea-like expanse of white, surging waves before them. In the blink of an eye the level ground reappeared, and he said to them, “You were fated to suffer several days of calamity. Now that the enchanted water is gone, return swiftly to camp and send men to Weizhou; only then can deliverance be obtained. Strive your utmost in the service of the state!” When he had finished speaking, he changed into a whirlwind and silently vanished. The company was endlessly astonished. Guarding Song Jiang, they made their way south. After traveling five or six li, they suddenly saw dust rising ahead. Another body of troops was coming from the south: Wu Yong, together with Wang Ying, Hu Sanniang, Sun Xin, Gu Dasao, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao, was leading ten thousand soldiers to their aid. Song Jiang said to Wu Yong, “Because I did not heed your counsel, worthy brother, we nearly never met again!” Wu Yong replied, “Let us return to the stronghold before we speak further.” They all entered the stronghold in order and gave a full account of their defeat, entrapment, and encounter with the deity. Wu Yong raised a hand to his brow and said, “The exalted power of wu and ji—that was a god of Earth. Your loyalty and righteousness, elder brother, moved the god of the Earth, and earth can subdue water.” Only then did Song Jiang and the others understand, and they bowed their thanks toward the heavens.

p.src: By then dusk was approaching. Some surviving soldiers straggled back and reported that, amid the confusion, Sun Qi, Ye Sheng, Jin Ding, Huang Yue, and others had opened the south gate of Zhaode and led troops in a sudden attack. A great many had been killed, while the rest had scattered and fled. Song Jiang mustered the soldiers and found that more than ten thousand had been lost. Wu Yong said to Song Jiang, “The rebels wield sorcery and have won two battles in succession. We must quickly devise precautions against a raid on our camp. Moreover, our soldiers are terrified: whether it be a bow’s reflection mistaken for a snake, the spectral guiche bird, wind imagined as troops, or grass as armored men, everything they meet will shake their resolve. We should leave this camp empty, with only sheep’s hooves beating the drums, while our main force withdraws ten li and establishes another camp.” Song Jiang at once gave the order for the army to withdraw ten li. Scholar Wu further had Vanguard Song order the camps to be divided: the great camps enclosing the smaller ones, their corners interlinked and their winding lines facing one another, after the method of Li Yaoshi’s Six-Flower Formation. The commanders obeyed.

p.src: They had only just finished establishing camp when word came that Fan Rui, obeying his orders, had ridden in haste from Huguan Pass. He entered the camp and paid his respects to Vanguard Song. After learning all the particulars concerning Qiao Daoqing, Fan Rui said, “Set your mind at ease, elder brother. It is nothing more than sorcery. Tomorrow I, Fan, shall work my arts and capture him.” Wu Yong said, “If he does not come to challenge us, we shall simply hold our troops here and make no move. We will wait until Gongsun Yiqing arrives before deciding what to do.” Song Jiang then ordered Zhang Qing, Wang Ying, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao to take five hundred light cavalrymen, ride through the pass that very night, and hasten to Weizhou to escort Gongsun Sheng back, so that he might defeat the enemy and deliver them. Zhang Qing and the others checked and readied their horses, took leave of Song Jiang, and departed. The Song troops planted their chevaux-de-frise deep, raised the stockades firmly, strung their bows, and drew their blades. Clad in armor, they slept upon their spears, passing watch-bells and calling the countersign. Song Jiang and the others kept candles burning as they waited for dawn; of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now Qiao Daoqing, having trapped Song Jiang with his magic, was just about to advance and seize him when he suddenly saw that not a drop of water remained ahead and that Song Jiang and his men had escaped. Deeply startled and perplexed, he said, “This art of mine is no trifling thing. How could he know at once how to break it? There must be some extraordinary adept in his army.” He thereupon recalled his troops, entered the city with Sun Qi and the others, and took his seat in the commander’s headquarters. Sun Qi and the others meanwhile prepared a celebratory banquet. The soldiers brought Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and Liu Tang, together with the previously captured Li Kui, Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, Li Gun, and Tang Bin, all bound, before the command tent. Standing to Qiao Daoqing’s left, Sun Qi caught sight of Tang Bin and cursed him: “Traitor! The Prince of Jin never wronged you.” Tang Bin shouted back, “The hour of your deaths has come!” Qiao Daoqing ordered them all to state their names. Li Kui opened his fierce eyes wide, bristled his tiger-like whiskers, thrust out his chest, and roared abuse: “Listen well, you thieving Taoist! I am your black grandfather, Li Kui the ‘Black Whirlwind’!” Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and the rest ignored his questions and, seething with anger, refused to say a word. Qiao Daoqing ordered the soldiers who had captured the fellows to be brought forward. Before long, the executioners escorted the soldiers in. After questioning them one by one, Qiao Daoqing learned that the captives were all valiant commanders in the Song army. He said to them, “If you are willing to surrender, I shall report to the Prince of Jin and have you all richly rewarded with official rank and title.” Li Kui bellowed like thunder, “What manner of men do you think we are? And yet you let out such bird-farts! If you want to hack your black grandfather to pieces, take me away and do it! Even if you strike me hundreds of times, should your black grandfather so much as knit his brow, he is no true man!” Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Liu Tang, and the others cursed in unison, “You sorcerous Taoist, cease your dreaming! The heads of us brothers may be severed, but these iron legs of ours will never bend!” Qiao Daoqing flew into a rage and shouted for them all to be taken out and beheaded, with a report to be made when it was done. Lu Zhishen laughed heartily. “I regard death as a homecoming. Today I shall die in a righteous cause.” The executioners crowded around them and led them away. Qiao Daoqing thought to himself, “Never in my life have I seen such unyielding men. I shall keep them alive for now and deal with them later.” Qiao Daoqing hastily issued an order for the soldiers to bring the band back and imprison them pending judgment. Wu Song cursed, “You filthy traitors! Hurry up and cut us down, and have done with it!” Qiao Daoqing lowered his head without speaking, and the soldiers took Li Kui and all the others away to prison.

p.src: Seeing that his art of the “Divine Water of Samadhi” had failed, Qiao Daoqing was already somewhat uneasy. He merely quartered his troops within the city and watched for news of the Song army’s movements. Thus both sides held their troops and made no move. Five or six days passed in succession. Nie Xin and Feng arrived with the main army, entered the city to pay their respects to Qiao Daoqing, and brought all their troops inside to encamp. Seeing the Song troops guarding their camp closely and refusing battle, Qiao Daoqing judged that they had no other scheme. He mustered his troops and, accompanied by his commanders Sun Qi, Dai Mei, Nie Xin, Feng, and others, led twenty thousand men out of the city at the fifth watch. They encamped at Five-Dragon Mountain south of the city and advanced at daybreak. Qiao Daoqing said to Sun Qi, “Today we must capture Song Jiang and recover Huguan Pass.” Sun Qi replied, “Everything depends upon the wondrous powers of Your Excellency, the Imperial Preceptor.” Qiao Daoqing then led ten thousand troops in an assault upon Song Jiang’s main camp. From a high rise, Qiao Daoqing surveyed the Song army’s encampment and saw:

p.src: In all four quarters and eight directions, every station was sure; front and rear, left and right, each could come to the others’ aid;

u.src: In all four quarters and eight directions, every station was sure; front and rear, left and right, each could come to the others’ aid;

p.src: The opening and closing of every gateway followed a method, and advance and withdrawal were coordinated in measured accord.

u.src: The opening and closing of every gateway followed a method, and advance and withdrawal were coordinated in measured accord.

p.src: Qiao Daoqing secretly applauded. Just then, a cannon sounded in the Song stronghold; the gates opened, and a formidable force surged out. Colored banners waved in both formations, and great war drums thundered to the heavens. Qiao Daoqing descended from the high ground and rode before the lines, with Lei Zhen, Ni Lin, Fei Zhen, and Xue Can guarding him on either side. As the standards in the Song formation parted, a commander galloped forth. It was Fan Rui, the Demon King Who Roils the World. Sword in hand, he pointed at Qiao Daoqing and cursed, “You villainous Taoist! How dare you run wild!” Qiao Daoqing thought to himself, “This man surely knows some magic. Let me test him.” He shouted at Fan Rui, “Ignorant, defeated wretch! How dare you spew such filth! Do you dare match your martial skill against mine?” Fan Rui replied, “If you want to test martial skill, come forward and take a stroke of my sword!” Both armies raised battle cries and beat their drums. Fan Rui spurred his horse, leveled his sword, and charged straight at Qiao Daoqing. Daoqing urged his horse forward and swung his sword to meet him. Two swords rose together as the two sorcerers battled. At first, the two horsemen remained locked together in combat. Then each employed his supernatural powers, and two streams of black vapor appeared, swirling left and right before the lines, tumbling wildly back and forth. The soldiers on both sides stared in amazement. When the fighting reached its height, Fan Rui spotted an opening and slashed at Qiao Daoqing. His sword struck only air, and he nearly toppled from his horse. Qiao Daoqing had deliberately exposed an opening to lure Fan Rui into striking, then used the Black Dragon’s Bone-Shedding Art. He had already returned before his own lines and was laughing heartily. Fan Rui returned to his lines in alarm.

p.src: The gate standards on both wings of the Song formation opened. From the left dashed Shan Tinggui, the General of Sacred Water, leading five hundred infantrymen, all under black banners and clad in black armor, armed with round shields, javelins, steel forks, and keen blades; from the right dashed Wei Dingguo, the General of Divine Fire, leading five hundred fire troops dressed in crimson and carrying incendiary weapons. Before and behind them rolled fifty fire carts, all loaded with reeds and other kindling. Each soldier had an iron gourd strapped to his back, filled with sulfur, saltpeter, and powders that made smoke of five colors; all were ignited at once. The two forces charged together—the left like black clouds sweeping over the earth, the right like soaring flames. The northern army, terrified, was about to retreat. Qiao Daoqing shouted, “Anyone who retreats will be beheaded!” Holding his precious sword in his right hand, he muttered an incantation. In an instant, black clouds covered the earth and wind and thunder raged. A shower of enormous hailstones descended, battering the Sacred Water and Divine Fire troops amid crashing thunderbolts and extinguishing every flame. The hail scattered the troops like falling stars and drifting clouds, and they fled in panic with hands over their heads. Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo were frightened out of their wits and knew not what to do. They barely escaped alive to their own formation; the “Sacred Water” and “Divine Fire” generals saw all their efforts come to nothing.

p.src: Presently, the hail ceased and the clouds withdrew, revealing once more a blue sky and bright sun; yet countless lumps of ice, some as large as hens’ eggs and others as large as fists, still covered the ground. When Qiao Daoqing looked toward the Song troops, he saw heads bruised and foreheads split, eyes blinded and noses awry; whenever they stepped on the ice, they slipped and fell. Flaunting his might and triumph, Qiao Daoqing cried aloud, “Is there anyone else among the Song soldiers with extraordinary skill and vast supernatural powers?” Fan Rui was overcome with shame and fury. With hair unbound and sword in hand, he stood upon his horse and exerted all the magic he had learned in his life, chanting an incantation. At once, wild winds rose on every side, sand flew and stones hurtled, heaven and earth grew dark with sorrow, and the sun lost its light. Fan Rui signaled his troops and charged forward. Qiao Daoqing laughed and said, “What can such paltry tricks of yours possibly accomplish?” He too raised his sword and worked his magic, muttering an incantation. The winds immediately turned and rolled wildly through the Song troops. Another thunderclap sounded in midair, and countless divine soldiers and heavenly generals came charging down. Horses neighed and men cried out in the Song formation as all fled about in confusion. Qiao Daoqing and his four subordinate commanders loosed their troops in pursuit and slaughter. Fan Rui’s magic failed him. Unable to hold out, he turned his horse and fled.

p.src: The northern army came on in pursuit, and at the moment of utmost peril, a beam of golden light suddenly shot from the Song stronghold. It dispersed the wind and sand, and all those heavenly soldiers and divine generals came tumbling down before the lines. When the men looked closely, they saw that they had been cut from colored paper. When Qiao Daoqing saw that his Divine Soldier Art had been broken, he fully displayed his powers. With hair unbound and sword in hand, he formed a seal with his fingers, chanted a spell, and cried, “Swiftly!” He then employed the Art of the Samadhi Divine Water. In an instant, countless streams of black vapor rolled in from the direction of north. A master in the Song formation suddenly galloped forth, wielding an ancient pine-patterned sword. He muttered an incantation and cried, “Swiftly!” Suddenly, many divine generals in yellow robes appeared in midair and flew northward, dispersing the black vapor. Qiao Daoqing was startled and knew not what to do.

Qiao Daoqing was startled and knew not what to do.

p.src: Seeing that this master had broken the sorcery, the Song troops all shouted abuse: “Qiao Daoqing, you sorcerous villain! Now someone of extraordinary skill has come to face you!” At these words, Qiao Daoqing blushed red to the tips of his ears and retreated toward his own formation. Qiao Daoqing had flaunted his supernatural powers all his life, but today he hung his head in dejection. Indeed: though all the waters of the Three Rivers were gathered up, they could not wash away the shame he suffered this day. But who was the master in the Song formation who broke the sorcery? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
